image_description: A single beige adhesive bandage (Band-Aid style) lying on a textured, light gray fabric surface. The bandage is oriented diagonally. It features a central white absorbent pad and tan adhesive wings with visible perforations. The lighting is soft, casting subtle shadows that suggest the object is resting on top of the fabric.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Small rectangular adhesive bandage of fingertip-to-finger-span length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The object clearly matches the scale and general shape of a standard adhesive bandage relative to the fabric weave texture.
The overall silhouette is a narrow rectangle with distinctly rounded corners, matching the taxonomy description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Central absorbent pad slightly raised above surrounding adhesive surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is a clear visual distinction between the central white pad and the tan adhesive areas. Shadows and highlights suggest the pad has slight thickness/relief compared to the flat adhesive wings.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Central absorbent pad surrounded by adhesive-coated fabric or plastic backing.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The structure shows a central pad flanked by two adhesive wings, which is the correct functional layout.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Protective paper strips cover adhesive side before use.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows the top side of the bandage (adhesive side up or non-stick side up depending on orientation, but likely top). Protective strips are on the underside and are not visible. Therefore, this checkpoint is untestable from this view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Thin and flexible conforming to body contours.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bandage is lying on a flat(ish) fabric surface, not applied to a body part. Its flexibility cannot be actively tested, though it appears thin.
The central pad is clearly white/off-white, contrasting with the tan backing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Backing material typically beige tan or transparent with perforated texture for breathability.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The backing is beige/tan. Upon close inspection, a fine grid/dot pattern consistent with perforation for breathability is visible on the tan areas.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Some variants feature printed patterns bright colors or character designs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is an optional variant feature. The specific instance shown is plain beige/white, so the feature is not present, but this does not fail the class definition.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The fabric background has a slightly 'smudged' or painterly quality where it meets the bandage shadow. The weave pattern becomes inconsistent and blurry near the contact points, suggesting minor generation artifacts in the interaction between object and background.

The left end of the bandage appears to merge slightly into the background shadow. The edge definition is softer than the right end, and the corner geometry seems to lose its crisp rectangular form, appearing slightly melted or ill-defined.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is correctly classified as a Band Aid and not a similar rectangular object like a label or patch.
To verify the boundary sharpness between the bandage and the fabric, checking for the edge bleeding/melting suspected by the Router.
To assess the overall realism of the fabric texture and lighting, and to detect any subtle global inconsistencies.

Consistency of the perforation texture on the adhesive wings
Realism of the fabric weave pattern surrounding the object
